::: {#sol-noise-second-moment}

@thm-variance says
$\Var{X} = \mathbb{E}[X^2] - (\mathbb{E}[X])^2$ for any $X$.
Taking $X = \noise$ and substituting $\mathbb{E}[\noise] = 0$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb{E}[\noise^2]
&= \Var{\noise} + 0^2 \\
&= \varpar
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-noise-second-moment}

so for mean-zero noise the average squared value *is* the variance.

The identity looks slight and does a lot of work.
@eq-noise-second-moment is the step that produces the irreducible error term
in regression and statistical modeling:
it converts a statement about the *spread* of the noise, which is what a
model of the world gives you, into a statement about *squared error*, which
is what the fitting objective measures.

:::
